-B.Name: -B
-B.description: Use suffix as the backup suffix if -b is given

-C.Name: -C
-C.description: Copy the file.  If the target file already exists and the files are the same, then don't change the modification time of the target

-S.Name: -S
-S.description: Safe copy. Normally, install unlinks an existing target before installing the new file. With the -S flag a temporary file is used and then renamed to be the target. The reason this is safer is that if the copy or rename fails, the existing target is left untouched

-b.Name: -b
-b.description: Back up any existing files before overwriting them by renaming them to file.old. See -B for specifying a different backup suffix

-c.Name: -c
-c.description: Copy the file.  This is actually the default.  The -c option is only included for backwards compatibility

-d.Name: -d
-d.description: Create directories.  Missing parent directories are created as required

-f.Name: -f
-f.description: Specify the target's file flags; see chflags(1) for a list of possible flags and their meanings

-g.Name: -g
-g.description: Specify a group. A numeric GID is allowed

-m.Name: -m
-m.description: Specify an alternate mode.  The default mode is set to rwxr-xr-x (0755). The specified mode may be either an octal or symbolic value; see chmod(1) for a description of possible mode values

-o.Name: -o
-o.description: Specify an owner. A numeric UID is allowed

-p.Name: -p
-p.description: Preserve the modification time. Copy the file, as if the -C (compare and copy) option is specified, except if the target file doesn't already exist or is different, then preserve the modification time of the file

-s.Name: -s
-s.description: Exec's the command strip(1) to strip binaries so that install can be portable over a large number of systems and binary types

-v.Name: -v
-v.description: Causes install to show when -C actually installs something

\u003cfile1 file2 | file1 ... fileN dire.Name: <file1 file2 | file1 ... fileN directory | directory ...>
\u003cfile1 file2 | file1 ... fileN dire.description: file1 file2 | file1 ... fileN directory | directory ...
